clue.text: Driver should check this contest with newspaper after engineers fail to start car?

indicators.note: after puts the contest, with and newspaper pieces behind the engineers and the shortened car

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps

indicators.note: failing to start means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: car is taken as written before its first letter goes
to vie is to contest or compete
the Mirror is a British daily tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A motoring tip, perhaps, about checking a car mirror while engineers and newspapers squabble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the contest, 'with' and newspaper behind the engineers; 'fail to start' beheads 'car'. RE is the Royal Engineers and the Mirror a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear-view mirror is the glass a motorist glances at to see traffic behind before manoeuvring.

clue.text: Watch half-cut group of drivers welcoming non-drinker for race meeting

indicators.note: half-cut keeps only the first half of the word, cutting the rest off

parts.note: to regard is to watch or look at

indicators.note: welcoming means the drivers' group takes the non-drinker inside it

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring breakdown organisation
TT stands for teetotal, a non-drinker

explanation.surface: A tipsy motoring club watches a teetotaller arrive at a race day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' (slang for drunk) here keeps the first half of 'regard'; 'welcoming' puts the teetotal letters inside the motoring group.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a series of boat races held as one sporting event.

clue.text: Raising stock value after banks withdraw supply with many brands hit briefly

indicators.note: read as 'supple-ly', in a flexible way, so the letters bend into a new order
the banks of a word are its outer letters, and once they withdraw only the inside is left

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: briefly cuts the word short by its last letter

explanation.surface: A financial report: stock value falls as banks pull out and big brands take a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising stock' sounds financial but means rearing farm animals. 'after banks withdraw' strips the outer letters of 'value'; 'briefly' docks 'hit'; 'supply' (as in supplely) shuffles everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal husbandry is the farming practice of breeding and rearing livestock.

clue.text: Video's margins upset film franchise

indicators.note: margins are the edges of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: the word video, whose margins are wanted

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's 1982 film E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial

explanation.surface: A video shop's edges curl while a film series hits trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'franchise' looks like a film series, but it is the right to vote. 'upset' turns ET into TE.
explanation.definitionFit: The franchise is the right to vote in elections, as in universal franchise.

clue.text: Queen on currency charge

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's royal cipher
the rand is South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: A queen's head on banknotes is something to charge for.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts ER above RAND.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a task one is charged with, a commission entrusted to someone.

clue.text: Changed — assuming the writer's in fashion with a bit of denim

indicators.note: in puts the conditional word and the pronoun inside the fashion word

parts.note: a mode is a fashion or style
if means assuming, on condition that
the writer refers to themself as I; the 's is 'is', joining to 'in'

indicators.note: a bit of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone altered their style, assuming they were trendy in denim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the writer's in' reads as 'I is in', so 'in' is the container signal; 'a bit of' takes the first letter of 'denim'.
explanation.definitionFit: Modified means altered or adjusted, a direct synonym for changed.

clue.text: 1 Across shows you this — ignoring France — European investment reveals what most politicians desire

indicators.note: ignoring tells us to drop the France letter from the word
investment of the European letter puts it into the gap that was left

parts.note: a rear-view mirror shows a reflection
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: A mirror image ignoring France and European investment shows what politicians crave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring France' removes F from REFLECTION; 'European investment' installs E in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Most sitting politicians hope to be voted back into office at the next poll.

clue.text: Surprisingly, most of army deem granola a breakfast favourite

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the letters turn up in an unexpected order
most of means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers, unexpectedly, mostly rate their granola as the best breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of army' gives ARM; 'Surprisingly' rearranges ARM + DEEM + GRANOLA + A.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange marmalade is a citrus preserve spread on toast, a staple of the British morning table.

clue.text: Arrest son once secret police force launches

indicators.note: launches means the police force sets off first, ahead of the son

parts.note: the Stasi was the secret police of the former East Germany

explanation.surface: A son is arrested when the old secret police launch a raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrest' looks like detention, but it is a noun meaning a halt; 'launches' puts STASI before S.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of standstill, an arrest of movement or growth.

clue.text: Flash, grand sedan

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand
a sedan chair is a litter, a carried enclosed seat

explanation.surface: A flashy, grand saloon car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sedan' looks like a saloon car but is the old carried chair.
explanation.definitionFit: Glitter is sparkle or showy brilliance, much like flash as a noun.

clue.text: Chaps regularly tucked into food made from mould

indicators.note: tucked into puts the picked letters inside the food word

parts.note: a diet is the food one eats

indicators.note: regularly picks alternate letters of the word, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Some men tucked into a meal set in a jelly mould.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the odd letters of 'Chaps'; 'tucked into' places them in the food word.
explanation.definitionFit: A die-cast object is shaped by pouring molten metal into a die, a mould.

clue.text: Warm up inside with a whiskey

indicators.note: inside says the answer sits within the following words

explanation.surface: Warming up indoors with a glass of whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'wiTH A Whiskey'.
explanation.definitionFit: To thaw is to melt or become warmer, so to warm up.

clue.text: Careless Greeks fined right away for critical points

indicators.note: careless handling scatters the letters into a new order
away means the right letter is taken out of the words

explanation.surface: Reckless Greeks are fined immediately for critical faults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' removes R from GREEKS FINED; 'Careless' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a knife-edge means a precarious, decisive point where things could go either way.

clue.text: Judgement sent masses haywire

indicators.note: going haywire is going wildly out of order, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A verdict sent crowds into chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment is an evaluation, the opinion reached on weighing something.

clue.text: A poltergeist making ordinary adult horrified

indicators.note: making one thing into another here means the ordinary letter is replaced by the adult letter

parts.note: a poltergeist is a noisy ghost
O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level
A is the film classification for adult

explanation.surface: A poltergeist turns an everyday grown-up into a terrified one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' turns the ordinary letter of the ghost into the adult letter, after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means struck with horror or shock.

clue.text: When people retire some workers will retain former government department money

indicators.note: retain means the workers hold the other letters inside

parts.note: worker bees, so bees are some workers
the DTI was the UK's Department of Trade and Industry, now abolished
M is short for money, as in M1 and M3

explanation.surface: When staff retire, workers keep money from an old government department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retire' suggests leaving work but means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedtimes are the hours at which people go to bed, retire for the night.

clue.text: Perhaps Cuban lives with both sides of lovable rogue at the start

parts.note: is means exists or lives

indicators.note: both here means the two side letters sit either side of the with word, holding it between them
the sides of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: and means with, together with

indicators.note: at the start picks the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Cuban lives with a charming rascal at the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: AND sits between L and E, the sides of 'lovable', then R from 'rogue' ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban lives on an island, Cuba, so is an example of an islander.

clue.text: Without principles he is one up as American returns to generate tension

indicators.note: returns says the whole string is read backwards
principles are principal letters, so without them each word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: An unprincipled man rises as an American comes back to build tension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without principles' strips the first letters to leave ESNEPS; with US added, 'returns' reverses the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is anxious uncertainty, the tension of waiting to see what happens.

clue.text: Succeeded with a fit, heavenly body

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
a turn is a fit or sudden attack, as in 'she had a funny turn'

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded through a fit, heavenly body that they have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavenly body' looks like a compliment to a fit person, but it is a planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn is a planet, and planets are bodies in the heavens.

clue.text: Gets on committees

definitions.meaning: to board a train or plane is to get on it
... are governing committees, such as ... of directors

explanation.surface: Someone advances in the world through committee work.
explanation.definitionFit: Boarding is getting onto transport, and a board is a body of directors or committee.

clue.text: Procedures coming from case of scurvy — crew losing one on board ship

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters
on board puts the shortened crew inside the ship

parts.note: SS is short for steamship

indicators.note: losing means the crew word drops the letter for one

parts.note: a crew is a team
A means one, as in 'a dog'

explanation.surface: Scurvy breaks out on a ship once a sailor goes missing.
explanation.walkthrough: TEAM loses A ('one') to give TEM, which goes 'on board' SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Systems are methods or established ways of doing things, like procedures.

clue.text: Throw up chocolate bar by the sound of it — getting jacket …

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to lob is to throw

indicators.note: by the sound of it says we want a word that is pronounced like the bar

parts.note: Aero is a British bubbly chocolate bar

explanation.surface: Vomiting chocolate over one's jacket, and continuing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw up' looks like vomiting; 'up' reverses LOB to BOL, then ERO sounds like AERO, a British chocolate bar. The ellipsis leads into 23 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolero is a short open jacket ending above the waist.

clue.text: Radio is becoming focus of syllabus for linguist

indicators.note: becoming means the word is in the radio turns into the new letters

parts.note: a transistor is a transistor radio

indicators.note: the focus of a word is its middle

explanation.surface: A radio is becoming central to the syllabus for language students.
explanation.walkthrough: IS in TRANSISTOR becomes LA, the middle letters of 'syllabus'.
explanation.definitionFit: A translator is someone skilled in languages who renders one into another.

clue.text: Lawyer content to leave burglars' fingerprints

parts.note: a DA is a District Attorney, an American lawyer

indicators.note: the content of a word is its inside letters; when they leave only the outer letters remain

explanation.surface: A lawyer is happy to leave the burglars' fingerprints at the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like satisfied, but it is the inside of 'burglars'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dabs is British slang for fingerprints, used by police.

clue.text: … spoils chocolate bar

explanation.surface: Continuing 20 Down: being sick spoils the chocolate bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars spoils or damages; a Mars bar is a well-known caramel and nougat chocolate bar.

clue.text: Ultimately Ed Sheeran's naked, dancing with date — it's one way to describe him

indicators.note: dancing moves the letters around into a new order
ultimately points to the last letter of the word
naked strips the word of its outer letters

explanation.surface: Ed Sheeran dancing naked with a date, and the clue describing him.
explanation.walkthrough: D (end of Ed) and HEERA (Sheeran stripped) are shuffled by 'dancing', then D for date follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ed Sheeran is a ginger-haired singer, so a red-haired person describes him.

clue.text: Flow out from faucet an American turned partially

indicators.note: turned says the hidden letters are read backwards
partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Water flows from an American tap, which is called a faucet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partially' picks ETANAME from the words; 'turned' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or stream forth from a source.

clue.text: Last of specials on menu is so complicated — including shelled oysters leads to incomprehensibility

indicators.note: including puts the shelled shellfish inside the rest
on means the special's letter comes next to the jumbled menu
complicated means tangled up, so the letters are rearranged
last of picks the final letter of the word
shelled removes the outer letters, the shell, of the word

explanation.surface: A restaurant menu so complicated that oysters leave diners baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' rearranges the menu words; 'on' adds the last of specials; 'including' takes in oysters 'shelled' of their outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mysteriousness is the quality of being baffling, hard to understand.
